title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache
quote: Drafter-side KV introduces additional GPU memory overhead.
proves: Block drafters (DFlash-style) keep a separate drafter KV: per-token KV rises 1.139x (Qwen3-4B, 144 KiB target + 20 KiB draft), 1.156x (Llama3.1-8B), 1.375x (Qwen3.5-27B), 1.8x (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B); drafter KV injection time grows 4.7x from 4 to 128 concurrent requests (Qwen3-8B); reusing target KV in place cuts KV utilization 4.3-24.6% and lifts peak throughput 5-17%.
does_not_prove: Draft overhead fraction grows as target KV shrinks (hybrid/MLA/GDN targets), but no study of how draft KV interacts with prefix caching, eviction, or offload tiers.
bearing: Supports draft-KV-elimination ideas; shows draft KV share is largest on hybrid models

title: Strong Drafts Need Compact Memories: Long-Context Speculative Decoding with Compressed KV Cache
quote: reduces draft-side memory by over 70%
proves: Independent drafter with adaptor-compressed KV cuts draft-side memory >70% with up to 2.08x (Llama3.1-8B) and 3.33x (70B) speedup at prefixes up to 32K.
does_not_prove: Single-request long-context focus; no batching, prefix-cache sharing or tiering of the compressed draft memory.
bearing: Threatens naive 'compress draft KV' candidates; already done

title: When Hidden States Drift: Can KV Caches Rescue Long-Range Speculative Decoding?
quote: KV-Reuse improves long-range acceptance, although end-to-end speedups remain marginal under current training pipelines.
proves: Letting an EAGLE-style drafter read the target KV (KVShot: hidden-only vs KV-only vs hybrid) raises long-range acceptance on Qwen3-8B but end-to-end speedup is marginal.
does_not_prove: Algorithmic study; no memory or serving-system accounting of drafter reading target KV.
bearing: Weakens 'draft reuses target KV for accuracy' as a speed win; memory angle open

title: vllm-metal: Speculative decoding
quote: Its committed KV and speculative lookahead share the Metal KV memory budget with the target.
proves: On the user's own backend, draft-model KV and lookahead share the target's Metal KV budget, no separate draft scratch pool; MTP reads target KV (no extra KV); with align-mode prefix caching drafts are capped at the state-block boundary. Methods: MTP, draft model, N-gram; DFlash/DSpark experimental.
does_not_prove: A search snippet of an earlier version said the draft KV cache was 'un-budgeted'; the current page says budgeted. No numbers on how much of the budget the draft takes.
bearing: Directly testable on M5 16 GB; supports measuring draft share of KV budget

title: [RFC]: Lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models (vLLM #50438)
quote: all of these EAGLE-style draft methods conservatively drop the last matched unit and recompute it.
proves: vLLM drops the last prefix-cache block for all use_eagle() methods because the draft input at a block boundary depends on the next token; one Qwen3.6 report (v0.20.1) saw hit rate fall 87.3% -> 69.9%, 1,056 fewer hit tokens per request. RFC proposes hashing one following token.
does_not_prove: Open RFC, not merged; cost on non-hybrid (16-token block) models is small and unmeasured here.
bearing: Supports 'spec-aware prefix cache keys' gap; also shows engines already working on it

title: [Bug/Perf]: the dense default chosen for Mamba + EAGLE reverts to 0% prefix reuse under interleaved long conversations (vLLM #58303)
quote: Under interleaved long conversations the pool fills, the attention chains get evicted, and prefix reuse returns to a clean **0%**
proves: Hybrid GDN + EAGLE/DFlash2 on RTX 5090: dense recurrent-state checkpoints (default chosen because EAGLE tail-block drop makes sparse retention unreachable) fill the pool; two alternating ~135K conversations get 0% reuse (55-65 s re-prefill) vs 97-99% with a 1-in-6 interval. Mamba page holds speculative state slots so block size moves with draft count (2176 at 7 drafts, 2432 at 15).
does_not_prove: Single reporter rig, hybrid models only; no policy study.
bearing: Strong support for spec-decode x prefix-cache capacity/eviction gap on hybrid models

title: EAGLE/MTP block drop + prefix caching is untested for hybrid models with >=3 attention groups (vLLM #51771)
quote: We hit a **total (0.0%) prefix-cache loss** on this configuration
proves: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark (4 attention groups): with EAGLE block drop on, 5-turn agentic session hit rate 0.0% vs 72.7% with drop disabled, wall clock 64.27 s vs 30.61 s, acceptance length 4.80 vs 4.76. CI covers at most 2 attention groups.
does_not_prove: Reported on a fork base; authors think main is fine for this shape. Test-coverage issue.
bearing: Supports gap: spec decode silently breaks prefix reuse; correctness/coverage tooling

title: [Bug] EAGLE speculative decoding defeats radix prefix reuse for multi-turn traffic (SGLang #32459)
quote: Enabling EAGLE speculative decoding collapses radix prefix reuse for multi-turn agentic traffic
proves: SGLang v0.5.16, GLM-5.2 NVFP4 8xB200: deep-prompt cache hit 97% without spec vs 53%/40% with EAGLE; input throughput 43,981 vs 12,881-16,811 tok/s; TTFT p50 0.54 s vs 2.15-2.68 s. HiCache on/off no effect. Candidate fix #32574 unmerged; issue stale-closed.
does_not_prove: One model family; root cause not confirmed.
bearing: Supports gap in SGLang radix cache + EAGLE; shows cost is TTFT not decode

title: [Bug] HiCache draft KV pool backup crashes with cudaMemcpyBatchAsync invalid argument in PD disaggregation (SGLang #31252)
quote: the draft KV pool's host backup crashes
proves: SGLang HiCache keeps a separate host-tier backup for the draft KV pool (mem_pool_host_draft) alongside the target pool; with PD + HiCache + EAGLE the draft-pool backup crashes (regression v0.5.14 -> v0.5.15).
does_not_prove: Bug report only; no data on host memory used by draft pool or its hit value.
bearing: Shows draft KV is tiered to CPU in SGLang; supports tiering-policy questions

title: HybridKVCacheCoordinator: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's ephemeral content incorrectly vetoes GPU-tier prefix cache reuse (vLLM #48455)
quote: It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an incrementally accumulated, reusable cache
proves: vLLM requires every KV group to hit; DSpark's draft group is rewritten each round from target hidden states, so it vetoes prefix reuse of the target's groups, including on resume after preemption. Contrasts with EAGLE/MTP draft KV, which is reusable.
does_not_prove: Open bug; no hit-rate numbers on GPU tier.
bearing: Supports taxonomy gap: which draft state is cacheable vs ephemeral

title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's sparse storage causes external_prefix_cache_hits_total to be permanently 0 (vLLM #47890)
quote: the external (RAM-tier) prefix cache **never records a hit**
proves: With CPU offloading, the draft group's stored blocks are sparse, so the AND-lookup returns 0 for every request even though target groups alone reach 88.9-100% hit rate, while offload store bytes grow into hundreds of GB.
does_not_prove: Specific to DSpark + OffloadingConnector; open.
bearing: Supports gap: offload tiers not designed for draft KV

title: [Bug]: Gemma 4 MTP + NIXL PD disaggregation - draft model KV not transferred, MTP ineffective (vLLM #54926)
quote: the draft model's KV state built during prefill is never transferred to the decode pod
proves: In vLLM PD disaggregation, draft KV groups are excluded from NIXL transfer; decode pod recomputes 15k+ tokens through draft heads per request at ISL=15k.
does_not_prove: No measured TTFT/throughput cost given.
bearing: Supports migration/transfer of draft state as an open systems gap

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: reduces KV cache capacity, limiting batch size and degrading throughput
proves: Keeping the draft model resident costs KV capacity; Nightjar offloads the draft to CPU when spec is disabled under memory pressure: up to 14.76% higher throughput and 20.18% lower latency.
does_not_prove: Moves whole draft model, not draft KV; abstract-level evidence.
bearing: Threatens 'offload draft when idle' candidate; already done

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
quote: equal parts, allocating one for the KV Cache of the draft model and the other for the KV Cache of the target model.
proves: Describes (older) vLLM lookahead scheduler splitting memory equally between draft and target KV caches.
does_not_prove: Refers to older vLLM; current V1 behavior not shown by this source.
bearing: Historic baseline for draft KV sizing; do not cite as current

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
quote: utilizes efficient suffix trees to cache long token sequences from prompts and previous outputs
proves: Model-free suffix-tree drafting caching prompts and prior outputs: up to 5.3x speedup, 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3, 1.9x over Token Recycling, on agentic SWE-Bench and Text-to-SQL.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no tree memory or CPU cost and no hit rates versus cache size.
bearing: Threatens basic cross-request draft cache ideas; leaves cache sizing/eviction open

title: Arctic Inference: Suffix Decoding docs
quote: Currently, only FIFO eviction is implemented.
proves: Global suffix tree of completed outputs plus per-request tree; suffix_cache_max_requests default 100000, FIFO eviction only; higher depth costs memory. Suffix alone: 286 vs 75.8 tok/s on SWE-Bench, 113 vs 76.0 on ShareGPT (vLLM 0.8.4).
does_not_prove: No memory size numbers, no hit-rate vs capacity curve, no tenant isolation.
bearing: Supports gap in eviction/admission policy for cross-request draft caches

title: SuffixDecoding at Production Scale with Arctic Inference and vLLM
quote: reduced memory by 2.3x
proves: Custom hashmap cut tree memory 2.3x and sped speculation 3.4x; original CPU cost 20-30 us/token, residual overhead about 10% at concurrency 64; original version was worse than n-gram at concurrency 64; 1.96-3.12x on BlazeEdit, 1.0-1.28x on SpecBench.
does_not_prove: No absolute tree size or hit-rate data.
bearing: Shows CPU-side draft cache cost matters at high batch size

title: [RFC]: Suffix decoding on GPU (suffix_gpu) - GPU-resident suffix decoding compatible with async scheduling (vLLM #51788)
quote: `method="suffix"` forces `--no-async-scheduling` today
proves: CPU suffix drafter needs committed host token ids, so it is excluded from async scheduling; RFC moves suffix automaton plus a cross-request global index onto GPU (capacity knobs suffix_gpu_global_capacity, delta_capacity).
does_not_prove: Proposal; GPU memory cost of the global index not quantified in the part read.
bearing: Supports question of where draft caches should live (CPU vs GPU memory)

title: REST: Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding
quote: results in a datastore with a size of 27GB
proves: Datastore sizes: 27 GB code (The Stack), 12 GB chat (UltraChat), 465 MB ShareGPT; retrieval 0.1-0.7 ms per token (<1 ms); 1.62-2.36x speedup at batch 1.
does_not_prove: Batch 1 only; static datastore; no tiering or update policy.
bearing: Baseline for size of retrieval draft caches; CPU/SSD placement open

title: Turning Trash into Treasure: Accelerating Inference of Large Language Models with Token Recycling
quote: requires \textless2MB of additional storage
proves: Adjacency matrix of past candidate tokens costs <2 MB and gives about 2x speedup across model sizes.
does_not_prove: No cross-request or multi-tenant sharing analysis.
bearing: Shows small draft caches suffice; weakens memory-pressure motivation for n-gram pools

title: Cacheback: Speculative Decoding With Nothing But Cache
quote: a fully populated table uses at most a few GiB of DRAM
proves: LRU n-gram tables (leader capacity 2^20, follower capacity 128) up to a few GiB DRAM; 1.86x on SpecBench Vicuna-7B with dynamic+frozen tables vs 1.64x dynamic only, 1.28x frozen only.
does_not_prove: No hit-rate numbers; dynamic cache is per task, not shared across requests.
bearing: Supports LRU-vs-FIFO and cross-request sharing as open questions

title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
quote: without needing auxiliary models or data stores
proves: Lookahead decoding: up to 1.8x on MT-bench, 4x with strong scaling on code completion, no auxiliary model or datastore.
does_not_prove: Abstract has no n-gram pool size or memory numbers.
bearing: Background for n-gram pool candidates

title: When Speculation Spills Secrets: Side Channels via Speculative Decoding In LLMs
quote: confidential datastore contents used for prediction
proves: Observers can fingerprint queries (>75% at T=0.3 over 50 prompts) across four spec schemes incl. vLLM, and leak datastore contents at >25 tokens/s; mitigations: packet padding, iteration-wise token aggregation.
does_not_prove: Does not study suffix-tree global caches shared across tenants specifically.
bearing: Threatens shared cross-tenant draft caches; supports isolation/partitioning candidates

title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
quote: employs a hierarchical 4-bit quantized KV cache and 4-bit quantized weights for acceleration
proves: Self-spec draft shares target architecture with hierarchical 4-bit KV and weights: >90% acceptance, about 2.5x speedup, about 1.3x less memory than sparse-KV self-spec.
does_not_prove: Long-context single-stream focus; no batching or prefix-cache interaction.
bearing: Threatens 'quantized KV draft' candidates; already done

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: SD can achieve speedup even for a high throughput inference regime for moderate to long sequences
proves: Sparse-KV draft gives up to 2.51x for Llama3.1-8B at batch 32-256 because KV, not weights, dominates at long context and large batch.
does_not_prove: Speedup depends on long sequences; short-context large-batch regime not helped.
bearing: Supports 'KV-bound regime' framing; threatens sparse-KV-draft novelty

title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
quote: dynamic sparse KV cache via retrieval as a draft model
proves: Hierarchical draft: target weights with retrieval-sparse KV, plus a small model drafting for it; 2.31x on A100 at 128K; offloaded on two RTX 4090 reaches 0.108 s/token, 4.86x over DeepSpeed-Zero-Inference on one 4090.
does_not_prove: Batch 1, no serving system integration.
bearing: Threatens sparse-KV and offloading spec candidates

title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
quote: speedup in decoding throughput over default vLLM
proves: Drafts with sparse attention over KV entries found critical during verification; 1.25-2.81x decode throughput over default vLLM, 1.15-1.29x over prior sparse self-spec.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not state memory cost or prefix-cache behavior.
bearing: Threatens sparse self-spec candidates in vLLM

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: has less memory footprint than other speculative decoding approaches
proves: Early-exit self-spec shares compute and activations (one KV cache) between draft and verify; up to 2.16x on CNN/DM, 1.82x coding.
does_not_prove: Needs special training; not a serving-system study.
bearing: Background for 'no separate draft KV' designs

title: SpecExec: Massively Parallel Speculative Decoding for Interactive LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
quote: we keep the past key/value caches of both draft and main models in GPU memory at all times
proves: Offloaded Llama 2-70B: 4-6 tok/s 4-bit, 2-3 tok/s 16-bit, up to 20 tokens per target iteration with draft budgets up to 2048; both KV caches kept on GPU, draft caches only needed during drafting.
does_not_prove: Batch 1; KV placement under memory limits only sketched.
bearing: Threatens spec-for-offload candidates; draft KV placement under offload open

title: Speculate Deep and Accurate: Lossless and Training-Free Acceleration for Offloaded LLMs via Substitute Speculative Decoding (SubSpec)
quote: delivering 9.1x speedup for Qwen2.5 7B on MT-Bench (8GB VRAM limit)
proves: Draft built from low-bit substitutes of offloaded layers; 9.1x Qwen2.5-7B (8 GB VRAM), average 12.5x Qwen2.5-32B (24 GB).
does_not_prove: Discrete GPU + PCIe setting, not unified memory like Apple silicon.
bearing: Threatens offload-spec candidates on discrete GPUs

title: ShadowSpec: Towards Zero Speculation Overhead for Substitute Speculative Decoding
quote: 17–54% end-to-end speedup over the SubSpec baseline
proves: Overlaps draft tree extension with PCIe loading of offloaded target weights: 17-54% over SubSpec on a consumer GPU.
does_not_prove: Workshop poster; PCIe-specific.
bearing: Shows offload-spec line is active as of 2026

title: Dovetail: A CPU/GPU Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding for LLM inference
quote: inference speedups ranging from 1.79x to 10.1x across different devices
proves: Draft on GPU, target on CPU: 1.79-10.1x on 13B models across devices.
does_not_prove: No memory figures on the page.
bearing: Background for heterogeneous placement

title: SGLang docs: Speculative Decoding
quote: the draft tree, CUDA graphs, and verification-related buffers consume additional VRAM
proves: SGLang has no separate draft memory knob; --mem-fraction-static covers weights + KV pool; NGRAM cache --speculative-ngram-capacity default 10,000,000 entries, max trie depth 18; NGRAM disables overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill.
does_not_prove: Docs do not mention radix cache compatibility or draft KV share of the pool.
bearing: Supports question on how engines size draft memory

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
quote: verification by the target model dominates the execution
proves: On vLLM across methods, workloads and batch sizes, verification dominates time, acceptance varies widely by position/request/dataset, and measured speedups fall well short of upper bounds.
does_not_prove: Abstract says nothing on memory effects.
bearing: Negative: caching draft state may be second-order next to verification cost

title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
quote: without permanently discarding the dense KV cache
proves: Training-free self-spec drafting from a dynamically sparsified, recallable view of the target KV; dense cache kept.
does_not_prove: No memory numbers on abstract page; speedup value missing from page text.
bearing: Threatens sparse-KV self-spec novelty (last 6 months)

title: vllm-ascend issue #9247 (DeepSeek-V4 MTP halves prefix-cache hit length)
proves: Search snippet only: enabling MTP cut prefix-cache hit length from 32768 to 16384 tokens due to EAGLE last-block drop plus alignment rounding.
does_not_prove: Not opened; numbers unverified.
bearing: Supports spec x prefix-cache gap on Ascend
